title: TimeFloats: Train-in-Memory with Time-Domain Floating-Point Scalar Products
problem: Compute-in-memory (CIM) lacks floating-point training capability; conventional ADC/DAC costly in advanced nodes
motivation: DNN training in memory attractive for efficiency; floating-point precision needed; ADC/DAC power/complexity limiting
method: TimeFloats performs floating-point arithmetic directly within memory, where data is stored, bypassing expensive analog-to-digital converters that translate continuous signals to numbers. It represents floating-point values using timing—the duration of electrical pulses—instead of voltage levels. The system uses purely digital logic, built using 15nm CMOS technology (a modern chip manufacturing process), to compute scalar products (multiplying pairs of numbers and summing them up).
key_novelty: The core innovation is encoding floating-point numbers through pulse timing rather than voltage level representation, enabling compute-in-memory training without requiring expensive analog-to-digital converters and achieving 22.1 TOPS/W.
